assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity via bifunctional degraders and molecular glues is a conceptually clean chemical idea (hijack the ubiquitin-proteasome system with a designed small molecule) that has opened previously undruggable targets and moved into clinical trials. Strong fit to molecular design with real translational reach.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies (with Sakamoto) made the original PROTAC concept; Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target underpins the molecular-glue half. Ciulli, Gray, Ito, Kim and others are important but a three-person set captures the conceptual origin plus the glue mechanism. Credit between PROTACs and glues is a compound-discovery split.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is independently confirmed in many labs and several degraders are in late-stage clinical testing; no approved PROTAC yet as far as I know, so timing is somewhat early but the chemistry is settled.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should treat PROTACs and molecular glues as one discovery or two.
Clinical approvals of bifunctional degraders remain pending to my knowledge; I have not verified current status.
Allocation among Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli and Gray is contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle of the cell reframed how intracellular compartments without membranes form. Originality and breadth are very high, and the physical-chemical framing (multivalency, condensates) suits a molecular-physics reading.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman showed P granules behave as liquids; Rosen provided the multivalent-interaction framework with synthetic systems. Pappu and Mittag contribute essential physical and sequence-grammar theory, so excluding them is a real allocation tension.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed across many systems, but debate continues about physiological relevance, the meaning of 'phase separation' versus other assemblies, and artefacts of overexpression; interpretation is still evolving.
uncertainties: Continuing controversy over in vivo relevance of condensates.
Credit distribution between cell-biology and biophysical-theory contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Programmable DNA self-assembly into arbitrary nanostructures (scaffolded origami, tile and brick methods) is an original, clear, widely adopted design paradigm for building matter at the molecular scale, directly relevant to biosensing and biomaterials.
assessment.attribution: Rothemund's 2006 origami is the decisive invention; Winfree provided algorithmic self-assembly and early collaboration with Rothemund; Yan contributed 2D/3D tile architectures. Seeman's foundational role is not in the credited names, and Shih and Yin are also strong, so credit is crowded.
assessment.maturity: Mature and reproduced worldwide; applications (drug delivery, nanoscale devices) are still developing, but the core discovery is stable and the timing is plausible.
uncertainties: Seeman's foundational contribution is not creditable here and he may be deceased, which complicates the story.
Many deserving contributors (Shih, Yin) for a three-person limit.
Practical impact is still emerging relative to the conceptual one.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation made total chemical synthesis and semisynthesis of proteins routine, enabling site-specific modifications, unnatural residues and probes. A clear, general chemical method with decades of impact in peptide and protein science.
assessment.attribution: Kent and Dawson introduced NCL in 1994; Muir developed expressed protein ligation, extending it to recombinant proteins. Danishefsky, Brik and Liu are important extensions but less decisive for the original concepts.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, validated and widely used for over 30 years; recognition is arguably overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Danishefsky, Brik and Liu are left out, which may be contested.
Boundary between NCL and expressed protein ligation as one prize topic.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically encoded unnatural amino acids via orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs allow rational chemical design of proteins in living cells. It is a foundational chemical-biology technology with broad use in biomaterials, probes and therapeutics.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and colleagues established orthogonal pairs in E. coli and eukaryotes (Wang was in the Schultz group); Chin extended to multi-site and quadruplet-codon reprogramming and engineered ribosomes. Mehl and Yokoyama contributed important systems.
assessment.maturity: Mature, reproduced and in routine use; therapeutic applications are emerging, so the science is established and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Division of credit between Schultz, Chin and Wang is delicate.
Mehl and Yokoyama contributions may deserve inclusion.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the enabling delivery chemistry behind siRNA drugs and mRNA vaccines, with extraordinary societal impact. Rational lipid design for nucleic-acid encapsulation and endosomal escape is clearly a chemistry-driven invention.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and Hope developed the lipid nanoparticle formation and ionizable lipid concepts; Anderson and Langer pushed lipid library discovery and materials design; MacLachlan and Madden were part of the early developments. Allocation is difficult and partly tied to corporate and patent histories.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at global scale; the delivery technology is mature, though the mRNA vaccine science itself was already recognized in Medicine, which may affect appetite for a related prize.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize for nucleoside-modified mRNA.
Contested attribution among Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite photovoltaics produced a remarkably rapid rise in solar-cell efficiency, a striking materials-chemistry story linking defect chemistry, optoelectronic physics and processing.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitized cells in 2009; Park developed the solid-state device reaching stable high efficiency; Snaith advanced the thin-film planar architecture. Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis also have major claims.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency is established, but long-term stability and commercialization remain open, so a prize now could be seen as early.
uncertainties: Broad claims by many groups make a three-person set contentious.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore sensing of single molecules, culminating in DNA and RNA sequencing, is a molecular-scale sensing platform of wide chemical and diagnostic impact, and relates to biosensing at the single-molecule level.
assessment.attribution: Deamer, Branton and Kasianowicz first showed nucleic-acid translocation; Bayley developed engineered protein pores; Akeson demonstrated controlled enzyme-ratcheted reading. Branton's possible death would limit the credit set.
assessment.maturity: Commercially mature and widely adopted; recognition would be timely, although the chemistry-versus-physics framing is mixed.
uncertainties: Priority and credit among Deamer, Branton, Kasianowicz, Bayley and Akeson are sensitive.
Whether the topic is better suited to another committee's perspective.
